correctness.rationale: A fixed-simplex-free simplicial self-map of a triangulated two-sphere would have fixed-point-free realization and hence degree -1 by Lefschetz. Nonzero degree forces a self-map of the same finite closed triangulated surface to be a simplicial automorphism. The low-order sphere classification leaves one four-vertex type, one five-vertex type, and two six-vertex types. Explicit fixed-simplex-free automorphisms eliminate the first three candidates; the remaining six-vertex stellar subdivision has exactly four automorphisms and every one fixes a simplex. The packaged checker exhaustively verifies all 6658 simplicial endomorphisms of that target and finds zero counterexamples.

value.rationale: Barmak’s existence theorem naturally raises the first-size question for the two-sphere, the first sphere dimension covered by that fixed-simplex construction. The theorem gives the exact onset, identifies a unique minimum combinatorial model, and supplies explicit failure witnesses for every competing smaller or equal-size type. This is a natural complete finite cutoff rather than an arbitrary parameter slice, and the minimum model is a useful benchmark for fixed-simplex decision procedures.
